gb-0Ton.title: Road lines: double yellow at the edge
gb-0Ton.summary: Double yellow lines along the edge of marked roads, mainly in towns, mean no stopping. Also found in Ireland.

gb-1NDu.title: Google car: white electric car, back visible
gb-1NDu.summary: Some Gen 4 coverage in London was taken by a white electric car with a distinct back. Similar cars were used in Dublin and Germany.

gb-36tt.title: Street sign: green townland line under the name
gb-36tt.summary: Signs with green text under the street name (the townland) are in western Northern Ireland, sometimes with a metal divider between the two lines in the north.

gb-5Q6L.hide: no learnable clue (only names the overseas territory and links a guide)

gb-5w6L.title: Street sign: plain blue with white letters
gb-5w6L.summary: Street signs in Aberdeen and Aberdeenshire are plain blue with white lettering. Central Aberdeen uses a black-and-yellow design.

gb-78cN.title: Houses: red brick
gb-78cN.summary: Red brick buildings are common in many parts. Also common in the Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark and parts of northern France.

gb-7Dwu.title: Plants: Cornish palm
gb-7Dwu.summary: Cornish palms (Cordyline australis) are most common in the far southwest along the coast and in Jersey, and rarely up the west coast to Scotland.

gb-7RAB.hide: no learnable clue (only names the overseas territory and links a guide)

gb-93V0.title: Sign: Twenty’s Plenty speed sign, green border
gb-93V0.summary: Speed signs with a green border and the words Twenty's Plenty are mostly in and around Glasgow.

gb-B2JD.title: Plate: white front, yellow back
gb-B2JD.summary: Front plates are white and back plates yellow. Most have no blue strip, some have a green Zero Emissions strip. Irish plates are white front and back with a blue strip.

differs.how: Irish plates are white both ends, always with blue strip

gb-Bhjy.title: Sign: give way sign says GIVE WAY
gb-Bhjy.summary: Yield signs say GIVE WAY. Irish ones say YIELD.

gb-C4hI.title: Lamppost: black sticker with yellow text
gb-C4hI.summary: Black stickers with yellow text sometimes appear on lampposts in Northern Ireland. Wiltshire has the same stickers.

gb-DOaW.title: Pole: wooden with metal crossbar triangle
gb-DOaW.summary: Poles sometimes have a metal crossbar near the top with two diagonal supports forming a triangle. Ireland, Sweden and Finland have similar ones.

gb-IJy2.title: Sign: black-white striped post with yellow bulb
gb-IJy2.summary: Pedestrian crossings are marked by a black-and-white striped post with a yellow bulb on top, not a sign. Very common in Ireland too.

gb-JAl0.title: Landscape: very hilly with bare rock, stone walls
gb-JAl0.summary: The Lake District is very hilly with lots of exposed rock and stone walls. It can look like the Scottish Highlands, which are usually less rocky.

gb-Jiou.title: Sign: diamond Passing Place sign
gb-Jiou.summary: Diamond-shaped Passing Place signs are mostly found in Scotland.

gb-MQvy.title: Sign: red-bordered triangle warning signs
gb-MQvy.summary: Triangular warning signs with a red border and white background, as in most of Europe. Ireland uses yellow diamonds.

differs.how: Irish warning signs are yellow diamonds

gb-MrGx.hide: no learnable clue (only names the overseas territory and links a guide)

gb-QHOv.title: Route marker: first digit shows the area
gb-QHOv.summary: A- and B-roads are grouped by first digit, so A380 and B3217 are in the southwest. Motorways follow the pattern. Think of a clock: digits go clockwise from 1 to 9. Roads starting 1 to 8 can also be in Northern Ireland.

gb-QKVV.title: Farm gate: square corners
gb-QKVV.summary: Rural metal gates have square corners. Irish gates usually have rounded corners, and Northern Ireland's do too.

differs.how: Irish farm gates have rounded corners

gb-Qaei.title: Bollard: yellow
gb-Qaei.summary: A yellow traffic bollard is commonly found.

gb-RDtH.title: Flags: the four national flags
gb-RDtH.summary: You sometimes see one of the four national flags, which tells you which part you are in.

gb-REyn.title: Road lines: long dashes with cat's eyes between
gb-REyn.summary: A middle line of long dashes with reflectors (cat's eyes) in the gaps is a good clue.

gb-RtMf.title: Bollard: round red-white with red-grey reflector
gb-RtMf.summary: Common in Scotland: a round, bulky red-and-white bollard with a red-and-grey reflector wrapping all the way round, sometimes elsewhere. Looks like a French one but its top is round, not spiked.

differs.how: French bollard top is more spiked

gb-UeRJ.title: Pole: yellow sticker with a person being zapped
gb-UeRJ.summary: Yellow warning stickers on poles show a person hit by a lightning bolt. Irish ones usually show just a bolt, often with an extra black-outlined sticker below.

differs.how: Irish stickers have no zapped person

gb-UmZq.title: Houses: chimney with several round pots
gb-UmZq.summary: Many buildings have chimneys topped with several round, brick-coloured pots.

gb-V5YP.title: Google car: Gen 2 only on a Channel island
gb-V5YP.summary: Jersey, between France and England, only has Gen 2 coverage. It counts as the UK for country streaks.

gb-Vq5E.title: Direction sign: blue, green or white with A or M
gb-Vq5E.summary: Direction signs can be blue, green or white. A and M are major roads, B smaller ones. Irish signs are bilingual with Irish names in italics.

differs.how: Irish signs are bilingual, Irish in italics

gb-WwWL.title: Street sign: low white sign on two posts
gb-WwWL.summary: White street signs with black text, placed low to the ground on two small posts. Suburban ones often have a small cul-de-sac icon. Some have other colours or crests.

gb-WwjT.title: Pole: wooden with metal step rods
gb-WwjT.summary: Wooden poles, often with thin horizontal metal rods bolted on as steps. Ireland has the same.

gb-X0Ns.title: Street sign: black, white outline, Rockwell font
gb-X0Ns.summary: Most street signs in the Wakefield council area are black with a white outline and letters, in the Monotype Rockwell Nova font.

gb-XahW.title: Pole: yellow tape or paint
gb-XahW.summary: Most poles and signposts in Birmingham have yellow tape or paint wrapped around them. Lampposts usually have the yellow sticker too.

gb-YFrb.title: Language: Gaelic clusters bh, dh, fh, mh
gb-YFrb.summary: Scottish Gaelic is closely related to Irish and uses accents. Look for bh, dh, fh, mh, ai, ea, eo and ui. On road signs it is mostly in the Highlands, north of Glasgow, and often in green or yellow text, which Welsh and Irish signs never use.

differs.how: Irish signs are never in green or yellow text

gb-ZTWS.title: Road marking: ARAF written in Welsh
gb-ZTWS.summary: Road markings are in English and Welsh. ARAF (Slow) is the most common and only found in Wales. Any clearly non-English marking next to an English one points to Wales.

gb-aUlL.title: Houses: terraced and semi-detached rows
gb-aUlL.summary: Terraced houses (rows sharing both side walls) and semi-detached houses (sharing one wall) are very common; about 61% of people live in them. Only Ireland and the Netherlands are similar in Europe.

gb-ecrT.title: Bollard: rounded, black ends, white stripe
gb-ecrT.summary: The most common bollard: rounded, black base and top with a white stripe in the middle, a red reflector on the front and a white one on the back.

gb-giuq.hide: no learnable clue (only names the overseas territory and links a guide)

gb-iLwq.title: Street sign: black name, red postcode and borough
gb-iLwq.summary: London signs show the street name in black, followed by the postcode and borough in red.

gb-j4to.title: Coverage: territory bordering Spain
gb-j4to.summary: Gibraltar is a British Overseas Territory at the southern tip of Iberia, bordering Spain. It counts as the UK for country streaks.

gb-lJbW.title: Google car: Gen 2 only on an island
gb-lJbW.summary: The Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, only has Gen 2 coverage. It counts as the UK for country streaks.

gb-lkL1.title: Pole: warning stickers wrapped around the pole
gb-lkL1.summary: Warning stickers wrapped all the way around the pole are specific to Northern Ireland. Mainland poles usually have one or two stickers.

gb-lm-10030.title: Bus stop: light blue UlsterBus sign
gb-lm-10030.summary: In Northern Ireland, most bus stops have light blue UlsterBus signs.

gb-lm-474348.title: Pole: wooden pole with flat top
gb-lm-474348.summary: France, Ireland and the UK can be hard to tell apart. Look at the tops of wooden poles: UK ones are flat.

differs.how: Irish wooden pole tops are slanted

gb-lm-490310.title: Kerb: striped kerbs on main roads
gb-lm-490310.summary: On the Isle of Man, striped kerbs can sometimes be seen along main roads.

gb-lm-513551.title: Bin: pink sticker, PEOPLE MAKE GLASGOW
gb-lm-513551.summary: A pink sticker saying PEOPLE MAKE GLASGOW is on trash bins in Glasgow.

gb-lm-515550.title: Guardrail: only A-type, no reflectors
gb-lm-515550.summary: Only A-type guardrails are used, which helps tell it from Ireland (A and B types).

differs.how: Ireland uses both A and B types

gb-lm-523150.title: Landscape: round hay bales on hilly fields
gb-lm-523150.summary: Round hay bales lying on hilly farm fields are mostly found north of Aberdeen and very rarely elsewhere in Scotland.

gb-lm-528828.title: Wall: dark grey stone, upright top stones
gb-lm-528828.summary: In Snowdonia, mostly south and north, roads have dark grey stone walls topped with vertical stones. The area is forested and mountainous, less so in the northeast. Similar walls appear elsewhere in North Wales.

gb-lm-530714.title: Coverage: boat trekker
gb-lm-530714.summary: Boat coverage exists in only three places: the River Thames in London, Keyhaven Lake and Loch Ness. Each has a different boat and landscape.

gb-lm-530778.title: Phone numbers: area code 0141
gb-lm-530778.summary: The landline area code 0141 is Glasgow.

gb-lm-530779.title: Phone numbers: area code 0131
gb-lm-530779.summary: The landline area code 0131 is Edinburgh.

gb-lm-530780.title: Phone numbers: area code 028
gb-lm-530780.summary: The landline area code 028 is all of Northern Ireland.

gb-lm-530781.title: Phone numbers: area code 0161
gb-lm-530781.summary: The landline area code 0161 is Manchester.

gb-lm-530782.title: Phone numbers: area code 0113
gb-lm-530782.summary: The landline area code 0113 is Leeds.

gb-lm-530783.title: Phone numbers: area code 0114
gb-lm-530783.summary: The landline area code 0114 is Sheffield.

gb-lm-530784.title: Phone numbers: area code 0151
gb-lm-530784.summary: The landline area code 0151 is Liverpool.

gb-lm-530785.title: Phone numbers: area code 0121
gb-lm-530785.summary: The landline area code 0121 is Birmingham.

gb-lm-530786.title: Phone numbers: area code 020
gb-lm-530786.summary: The landline area code 020 is London.

gb-lm-530788.title: Phone numbers: area code 029
gb-lm-530788.summary: The landline area code 029 is Cardiff.

gb-lm-542428.title: Plate: black with a letter and 3 numbers
gb-lm-542428.summary: A distinctive black plate with one letter followed by three numbers, in white or yellow, sometimes mixed. Common in Cornwall.

gb-lm-542625.title: Road lines: gaps in the lines
gb-lm-542625.summary: Gaps in road lines are most common in Wales.

gb-lm-542893.title: Houses: terraced hillside valley, pastel trim
gb-lm-542893.summary: The big valley northwest of Cardiff has many terraced houses, brown stone walls and colourful windows, often with pastel shapes around windows and doors. The towns are on hills. Similar valleys elsewhere in Wales are smaller.

gb-lm-542950.title: Pole: orange tape and white sticker with diamond
gb-lm-542950.summary: In Northamptonshire, orange tape is often wrapped around poles, plus a white sticker with blue text, numbers and a diamond icon.

gb-lm-543004.title: Sticker: colourful pole sticker
gb-lm-543004.summary: Colourful stickers in the Western Isles, rarely seen as there are few lampposts. They show up in Stornoway and occasionally elsewhere.

gb-lm-543005.title: Pole sticker: yellow, 6-digit code and QR code
gb-lm-543005.summary: A yellow sticker with a 6-digit code then a QR code, found on rural wooden poles in counties north of London: Norfolk, Suffolk, Essex, Cambridgeshire, Bedfordshire, Hertfordshire and Buckinghamshire.

gb-lm-543123.title: Bus stop: M logo, phone code, bee
gb-lm-543123.summary: The Greater Manchester bus stop sign has a phone code and an M logo top left, and a bee on the right, on one side only. Older ones are all white with a huge M.

gb-lm-543234.title: Pole sticker: white, numbers in a T shape
gb-lm-543234.summary: A white sticker with numbers forming a T shape is found in Pembrokeshire and Carmarthenshire.

gb-lm-543390.title: Street sign: says City of Southampton
gb-lm-543390.summary: Southampton street signs almost always have the words City of Southampton on them, all over the city.

gb-lm-543391.title: Pole sticker: white, blue letters, phone number
gb-lm-543391.summary: A white sticker with blue numbers and letters, often with a phone number below, is found in Suffolk.

gb-lm-543392.title: Street sign: L at the bottom right
gb-lm-543392.summary: Liverpool street signs often have an L in the bottom right corner. In the centre, signs have a unique shape and often say City of Liverpool.

gb-lm-543553.title: Street sign: BS and a number on the right
gb-lm-543553.summary: Bristol street signs always show BS and a number on the right. BS is for Bristol.

gb-lm-543554.title: Street sign: LS and a number on the right
gb-lm-543554.summary: Leeds street signs always show LS and a number on the right. LS is for Leeds. A different sign only appears in the centre.

gb-lm-543680.title: Landscape: wooded hills with towers to the west
gb-lm-543680.summary: In Belfast you often see wooded hills, balder on top, to the west and northwest, sometimes with one or two towers, and hills to the east and southeast. Once you know it's Northern Ireland, it is certainly Belfast.

gb-lm-543805.title: Landscape: treeless grassy hills, no mountains
gb-lm-543805.summary: The Shetland Islands have very little vegetation, usually no trees, no mountains, only grassy hills with small bushes. Some parts look like the Faroe Islands.

gb-lm-544405.title: Pole sticker: white, 1-2 numbers, small text
gb-lm-544405.summary: A white sticker with one or two numbers and lots of small text with a logo below, found in Hampshire and West Sussex. Sometimes there is text and a logo above, or only text without a number.

gb-lm-544553.title: Pole sticker: yellow with LCC under the numbers
gb-lm-544553.summary: Yellow stickers with LCC (Lincolnshire County Council) under the numbers mean Lincolnshire. If only CC is clear, that also confirms it. North Lincolnshire and North East Lincolnshire are separate councils.

gb-lm-545000.title: Pole sticker: white, FAULT and phone number
gb-lm-545000.summary: A white sticker with one black letter and four numbers, and FAULT with a phone number below, is found in Perth and Kinross, usually in a small frame.

gb-lm-545316.title: Pole sticker: white with diamond and small text
gb-lm-545316.summary: A white sticker with black letters and numbers and a diamond with small text underneath is found in Cambridgeshire, Coventry, Derby and South Tyneside. Derby always has 7 characters and no gap; South Tyneside has a blue sticker beneath; Peterborough has its own PCC sticker.

gb-lm-545436.title: Landscape: lots of sheep in hilly hedged fields
gb-lm-545436.summary: Sheep are most common in Wales but can be anywhere. Lots of sheep in hilly or mountainous land with hedgerows and green fields is a fair guess for Wales.

gb-lm-545569.title: Landscape: rocky, treeless, tundra-like
gb-lm-545569.summary: Around the Hebrides the land is often rocky, treeless and tundra-like, mostly seen in the Western Isles.

gb-lm-545710.title: Bus stop: distinct logo on top
gb-lm-545710.summary: Greater London bus stop signs have a very distinct logo on the top half.

gb-lm-545782.title: Landscape: treeless open farmland, small hills
gb-lm-545782.summary: The Orkney Islands are mostly treeless and open with vast farmland and small hills.

gb-lm-546439.title: Houses: Tudor black-and-white timber
gb-lm-546439.summary: Tudor-style black-and-white buildings, sometimes with red brick, are mainly in the West Midlands and East Anglia, near the Welsh border, and fairly common in the south (Kent, Sussex, parts of Surrey and Oxfordshire). Rare in northern England, almost never in Scotland.

gb-lm-546442.title: Plants: dense pine forest
gb-lm-546442.summary: Kielder Forest and nearby areas are full of dense pine trees, more than anywhere else.

gb-lm-546443.title: Houses: white with black corner frames
gb-lm-546443.summary: Around Keswick in Cumbria, white houses often have black ladder-like frames at the corners and black frames around windows. Found elsewhere too.

gb-lm-546444.title: Bus stop: distinct logo on top
gb-lm-546444.summary: West Midlands County bus stop signs have a very distinct logo on the top half.

gb-lm-546593.title: Houses: stone and pastel with coloured trim
gb-lm-546593.summary: Many Welsh towns mix stone and pastel buildings with colourful paint around doors and windows, especially near the west coast. South West England can look similar.

gb-lm-546747.title: Houses: dark red brick, black-white lintels
gb-lm-546747.summary: Around Manchester and Lancashire, lots of dark red brick, dark brown, black and white doors, and black-and-white lintels over windows. Dark red brick appears elsewhere too.

gb-lm-549735.title: Houses: red brick garden walls with garage doors
gb-lm-549735.summary: Around Newcastle, red brick walls extend from houses to enclose gardens, often with garage doors built in.

gb-lm-549736.title: Wall: very hilly national parks with stone walls
gb-lm-549736.summary: The Lake District, North Pennines, Yorkshire Dales, Nidderdale and Peak District are hilly with most of the stone walls. The Lake District is the hilliest with bare rock; it, the North Pennines and the Dales sometimes have abandoned-looking barns.

gb-lm-549737.title: Landscape: brown rolling moorland
gb-lm-549737.summary: The North York Moors have rolling, mostly brown moorland with rough grass and low plants.

gb-lm-549738.title: Houses: dark gritstone with black patches
gb-lm-549738.summary: The Pennine areas of Yorkshire and Lancashire often have dark gritstone with black patches on the bricks, more towards the south.

gb-lm-549739.title: Houses: industrial brick, factories, warehouses
gb-lm-549739.summary: Midlands towns, especially around the Black Country and Birmingham, look industrial with factories, warehouses and old brick buildings.

gb-lm-549740.title: Landscape: very flat, dikes, few hedgerows
gb-lm-549740.summary: Eastern England is flatter. The Fens, reclaimed land, look Dutch: very flat and open, straight roads and small dikes, hedgerows often absent. The area around Goole is similar.

gb-lm-551997.title: Roofs: red clay pantiles
gb-lm-551997.summary: Red clay pantile roofs, especially on older houses, are common along the eastern coast from Fife down to East Anglia.

gb-lm-551998.title: Gardens: neat gravel front gardens
gb-lm-551998.summary: Lincolnshire, Norfolk and the Fens often have bungalows with neat gravel front gardens.

gb-lm-551999.title: Houses: golden limestone
gb-lm-551999.summary: Golden limestone is very common in and around the Cotswolds, especially to the north.

gb-lm-552001.title: Roofs: thatch
gb-lm-552001.summary: Thatched roofs are most common in the middle of southern England, especially around Hampshire and Wiltshire.

gb-lm-552002.title: Landscape: forest mixed with heathland
gb-lm-552002.summary: The New Forest has a distinctive look, a mix of forest and heathland.

gb-lm-552003.title: Houses: hanging tiles on walls
gb-lm-552003.summary: Weald hanging tiles (tiles covering walls) are most common in Sussex and Kent, sometimes elsewhere in southern England.

gb-lm-552004.title: Wall: pebble or flint with red brick
gb-lm-552004.summary: Houses and walls of pebbles or flint with red brick built in are found in East Anglia, most commonly Norfolk, and in southern Sussex and East Sussex. The stones can rarely be yellow or black.

gb-lm-552005.title: Houses: big gated mansions on leafy roads
gb-lm-552005.summary: Wealthy areas near London, especially Surrey and Berkshire, have big houses and gated mansions on leafy roads.

gb-lm-554501.title: Pole sticker: white, 2 black numbers, small text
gb-lm-554501.summary: A white sticker with two black numbers and three pieces of small text, one above and two below, is found in Fife.

gb-lm-554502.title: Pole sticker: yellow on another white sticker
gb-lm-554502.summary: A yellow (sometimes white) sticker with 3 numbers and 4 numbers beneath, pasted on a white sticker behind it, is found in Ceredigion.

gb-lm-555609.title: Pole sticker: blue stickers
gb-lm-555609.summary: Stickers with blue (not just blue text) are in North Wales: light blue in Anglesey, green-white-dark blue in Denbighshire, purple-white-light blue in Conwy, generic blue in Flintshire, Wrexham and rarely Gwynedd.

gb-lm-555891.title: Wall: castle-like stone walls
gb-lm-555891.summary: Stone walls that look like castle walls are mostly in North Wales, especially on and towards Anglesey, and sometimes elsewhere in Wales.

gb-lm-557137.title: Landmark: Gulliver the seagull
gb-lm-557137.summary: A statue called Gulliver the Seagull means Colwyn Bay.

gb-lm-634015.title: Plate: white front, yellow rear, red strip
gb-lm-634015.summary: Like the UK, white front and yellow rear plates, but with a red strip on the left.

gb-lm-766561.title: Landscape: small hilly area, rock walls
gb-lm-766561.summary: A small region at the far south of the Mournes area is slightly hilly with lots of rock walls and distinct mountains to the north. Further west there are hedgerows instead of walls but the same mountains.

gb-lm-766562.title: Landscape: very flat with big hedgerows
gb-lm-766562.summary: Big hedgerows with very flat land point to north-eastern East Anglia. Normal hedgerows with flat land are also a good clue.

gb-lm-766564.title: Pole sticker: black eagle logo on top
gb-lm-766564.summary: A unique sticker with a black eagle logo on top is found in Bedford and around it.

gb-lm-766662.title: Landscape: hills with few mountains
gb-lm-766662.summary: The northern Highlands are much less mountainous than the rest, mostly hills, with a few or no mountains in the distance.

gb-lm-787158.title: Language: English
gb-lm-787158.summary: English is the main language. It is also spoken in Ireland, Malta and Gibraltar in Europe.

gb-qc5P.title: Language: Welsh, many D, W, Y and LL
gb-qc5P.summary: Welsh is spoken across Wales and road signs are usually bilingual. It uses D, W and Y a lot, and the double LL is distinct. Scottish Gaelic and Irish look somewhat similar.

differs.how: Irish is a different Celtic language that looks similar

gb-rm9B.title: Landscape: barren high mountains
gb-rm9B.summary: The Scottish Highlands are semi-barren and very mountainous. Much Gen 4 coverage is from early spring, so plants look brown and yellow. The most mountainous parts of Wales and northern England can look similar.

gb-rwuG.title: Houses: identical suburban semis, cul-de-sacs
gb-rwuG.summary: Suburbs have near-identical, often semi-detached houses with neat lawns and a maze of cul-de-sacs and curvy roads.

gb-uMg6.title: Driving side: left
gb-uMg6.summary: Drives on the left. Ireland, Malta and Cyprus are the only other European countries that do.

gb-vT4m.title: Google car: low camera, big round blur
gb-vT4m.summary: A low-mounted Gen 4 camera with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be see-through, which makes it easy to miss.

gb-vY5y.title: Landscape: green fields, hedgerows, low hills
gb-vY5y.summary: Very green countryside with many hedgerows beside the road and low rolling hills. Ireland looks very similar.

gb-wdhk.title: Houses: black-and-white timber framing
gb-wdhk.summary: Some old and new buildings have black-and-white timber framing. Less common in Ireland.

gb-wqNg.hide: no learnable clue (only names the overseas territory and links a guide)

gb-xFi3.title: Bin: city name on it
gb-xFi3.summary: Bins in towns often have the city name written on them.

gb-yII8.title: Phone numbers: area codes, 020 and 028
gb-yII8.summary: Landlines have nine or ten digits after the 0, and the first two to four are the area code. Geography is mostly random, but big-city codes are worth learning. All of London uses 020 and all of Northern Ireland 028.

gb-zRI4.title: Chevron: black with white arrows
gb-zRI4.summary: Black chevrons with white arrows. Irish ones are black with yellow arrows, French ones blue with white.

differs.how: French chevrons are blue with white arrows

gb-zdZe.title: Houses: big blocks of sandstone or granite
gb-zdZe.summary: Houses of large sandstone or granite blocks are common in Scotland. Granite in Aberdeen, red sandstone in Glasgow and Dumfries, yellow sandstone in Edinburgh.
